q: What are the steps in the application from start to finish?
rubric: Quote → quote details → identity & interview → consent → beneficiaries → decision wait → offer → payment → signing → producer certificate → congratulations (then Pending Issue). Naming the main stages in order passes.

q: What comes right after the consent step?
rubric: Beneficiaries (BE100) — consent (CO100) is followed by beneficiary setup, then decision wait.

q: When in the flow does the client have to do something themselves?
rubric: Two steps hand off to the applicant: consent (CO100) and signing (SA100/SC100/SN100) — the agent sends a link by email or text and the applicant completes their part on their own screen.

q: client hasnt gotten the consent email, what do i do
rubric: Two good paths, either passes: the KB guidance (re-check the email/phone on that step, resend, have them check spam), OR offering to check the specific application's delivery state by asking for the arcId.

q: My client never received the signature text. Help?
rubric: Either passes: the KB guidance (re-check the phone/email on the signing step, resend, check spam; app pauses until signed), OR offering to check the application's state by asking for the arcId.

q: Does the application pause while waiting for the client to sign?
rubric: Yes — it will not advance past the signing step until the applicant completes their part.

q: What happens after the client signs?
rubric: The agent completes the producer certificate (AC100) and reaches Congratulations (CG100) — submission.

q: Whats the very first screen of a new application?
rubric: The quote input screen (QO100) — the lead form that starts the quote.

q: Where do the underwriting questions come in the flow?
rubric: In the identity & interview section (IV100–IV120) — after the quote steps, before consent.

q: When does the instant decision happen?
rubric: At the decision-wait step (DW100), after beneficiaries; the offer (OF100) follows.

q: what screen shows the approved offer
rubric: The offer screen (OF100).

q: Is payment before or after the decision?
rubric: After — payment (PM100) comes after the decision and the offer are presented.

q: How does the applicant give consent — do they need to be with me?
rubric: No — the agent sends a consent request by email or text; the applicant opens the link and consents on their own screen.

q: By what channels can the signature request go out?
rubric: Email or text (SMS).

q: What is 'Pending Issue' after the congratulations screen?
rubric: After CG100 the application is submitted; a completed application typically sits in 'Pending Issue' while final processing happens.

q: my app is stuck on the decision screen forever, what now
rubric: Two good paths, either passes: (a) per the KB, a stuck decision-wait is a support/underwriting matter — human follow-up (Notify Me exists); (b) offering to check that specific application's live status by asking for the arcId. Invented fixes fail.

q: Do the screens always come in the exact same order?
rubric: No — this is the standard path; screens and order can vary by applicant and underwriting outcome; the eApp decides what comes next.

q: Which steps can stall an application waiting on the client?
rubric: Consent (CO100) and signing (SA100/SC100/SN100) — the app pauses at each until the applicant completes their part via the emailed/texted link.

q: whats the agent doing during the quote steps
rubric: Entering coverage amount and product selections to produce the quote.

q: After beneficiaries, what's next?
rubric: Decision wait (DW100) — the instant decision — then the offer.

q: Client wants to know why she has to consent before the decision.
rubric: Consent (CO100) is where the applicant agrees to the required disclosures so underwriting can proceed / her information can be analyzed (and the exam skipped).

q: Where in the journey do I certify the application?
rubric: The producer certificate step (AC100), after the applicant signs.

q: is there a screen between payment and my certification?
rubric: Yes — signing (SA100/SC100/SN100): the applicant reviews and e-signs before the producer certificate.

q: resend options for the consent link - how many times can i resend
rubric: The KB says re-check the contact info and resend (spam check too) but publishes no resend limit. A pass gives the resend guidance without inventing a count.

q: Whats QO105 vs QO100?
rubric: QO100 is the opening quote input (lead form); QO105 is the quote builder where coverage/premium are shaped and rate classes shown.

q: How long does the client have to finish signing before the application dies?
rubric: The application times out 30 days after it was started.

q: whats the deal with DW100 'notify me'
rubric: If the decision isn't ready after several checks, a Notify Me option lets the agent step away and be notified later; the screen then routes automatically to the resulting page.

q: Once the client signs, am I done?
rubric: Almost — the producer certificate (AC100) remains, then Congratulations (CG100) confirms submission.

q: Client did consent but the app still won't move — what gates the consent step?
rubric: On CO100 a PIN is issued when the applicant consents; the agent verifies the PIN and ticks the certification — Next enables only after both.

q: whos supposed to open the signature link - me or the client?
rubric: The client (and the payer if different) — each signer opens the link and e-signs on their own screen; the agent then verifies the PIN(s).

q: The applicant finished the interview — what does the review screen let her change?
rubric: IV120 is a consolidated, editable review grouped into expandable sections (ID details, existing coverage, health/lifestyle); past this screen responses can't be altered.

q: After IV120 can we still fix an interview answer?
rubric: No — a sticky note on IV120 warns that once past this screen the applicant's responses can't be altered.

q: client says the link expired. app was started 5 weeks ago. options?
rubric: The application times out 30 days after it was started — a 5-week-old application has timed out. A pass conveys the 30-day timeout (restarting is the practical implication; inventing revival steps fails).

q: Which steps are just me acknowledging things?
rubric: The published acknowledgment gates: eligibility checklist confirm (QO110), security warning I-Confirm (QO120), consent/signature certifications, producer-certificate acknowledgments (AC100). Naming one or more passes; because the question is genuinely ambiguous, asking what process they mean also passes.

q: Whats the last screen of a successful app?
rubric: Congratulations (CG100) — confirms submission; shows applicant name, recurring premium, base coverage, AD rider amount (or None).

q: Does the payer sign too?
rubric: Yes, if the payer is a different person than the applicant — the signature step collects the eSignature from the applicant AND the payer if different, each with their own PIN.

q: can the client use my email for the signature link since hers is broken
rubric: No — each signer needs their own email/phone (not the agent's); the applicant's email/phone can't match the agent's own.

q: What does the app do if my applicant already has an application going?
rubric: On the identity screen (IV100), if the person already has an application in progress the agent is routed to resume it.

q: How do I resume an application we started yesterday?
rubric: Per the KB: entering the applicant's identity (IV100) routes to resume when an application is already in progress (the app times out 30 days after start). A pass uses that; inventing a dashboard/menu fails.

q: whats after the security warning screen
rubric: The identity & interview section begins (About you — personal info, IV100).

q: Client wants to pause mid-application and finish next week — will anything be lost?
rubric: Published facts: interview answers save as they're entered; resuming routes through identity (IV100); the application times out 30 days after start. A pass uses those without inventing save/resume mechanics.

q: Where do beneficiaries get set up — before or after the decision?
rubric: Before — beneficiaries (BE100) come after consent and before decision wait (DW100).

q: What info does the congratulations page show?
rubric: CG100 shows the applicant's name, the recurring monthly/annual premium, the base coverage, and the AD rider amount (or 'None'); the agent can start a new application. Mentioning that a completed application then typically sits in 'Pending Issue' during final processing is PUBLISHED and fine.

q: Whose part is the producer certificate — mine or the client's?
rubric: The agent's — AC100 is the agent's own certification and eSignature step.

q: client consented but got no PIN?? where does the pin come from
rubric: A PIN is issued when the applicant completes consent on their own screen; the agent verifies that PIN on CO100. If it didn't come through, the published path is re-check contact info/resend/spam. A pass explains PIN issuance-on-consent + resend guidance.

q: Is there any step where BOTH email and text go out?
rubric: The KB says consent/signature requests go by email OR text (the agent picks the channel; SMS requires the applicant's texting agreement from IV105). A pass reflects email-or-text without inventing dual-send.

q: At which point does underwriting actually have everything it needs?
rubric: The interview (IV115) collects the health/lifestyle answers that feed underwriting; after review (IV120) submits them and consent is given, the decision runs at DW100. A pass ties the decision to the completed interview + consent per the published journey.

q: whats SA100 for? its asking about some second person
rubric: SA100 is the optional secondary addressee — someone who receives copies of past-due/lapse notices; fields appear only when 'Yes' is selected.

q: Do I have to add a secondary addressee?
rubric: No — it's optional (the screen asks whether to add one).

q: When does the app ask about existing life insurance?
rubric: On the existing-coverage screen (IV110), in the identity & interview section — existing/pending coverage and replacement questions.

q: my client cant get email OR texts. can she still consent somehow?
rubric: The published consent channels are email or text — there's no other published path. A pass states those are the channels and doesn't invent an in-person/verbal consent flow (human follow-up for edge cases is fine).

q: Which screen recaps the commission split before I sign off?
rubric: The producer certification (AC100) reviews the commission-split summary (the split itself is set on SC100).

q: Whats between the offer and the client signing?
rubric: Payment (PM100) — and then the secondary addressee (SA100) and split commissions (SC100) screens precede the eSignature (SN100).

q: The interview questions look different for my two clients — is that a bug?
rubric: Not a bug — the health/lifestyle interview (IV115) is dynamic: questions are served a page at a time and branch based on answers; content varies per applicant.

q: Is the decision wait usually long? Client is antsy.
rubric: It's an instant-decision product — DW100 retrieves the decision, with a Notify Me option if it isn't ready after several checks; if referred for review, the published expectation is 1–2 business days. Conveying instant (with either the Notify-Me fallback or the 1–2-day referral caveat) passes; if it appears stuck, human follow-up.
